'''Dame Clare Philomena Grey''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|DBE|FRS}} is Geoffrey Moorhouse Gibson Professor in the [[Department of Chemistry, University of Cambridge|Department of Chemistry]] at the [[University of Cambridge]] and a [[Fellow]] of [[Pembroke College, Cambridge]]. Grey uses [[nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy]] to study and optimize [[Electric battery|batteries]].

==Education==
Grey received a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree in 1987 followed by a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree in [[chemistry]] in 1991, both from the [[University of Oxford]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Clare P. Grey|url=https://www.ampere-society.org/index.php?page=grey|url-status=live|website=Groupement Ampere|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624202522/https://www.ampere-society.org/index.php?page=grey |archive-date=24 June 2021 }}</ref> Her doctoral thesis, under the supervision of Sir [[Anthony Cheetham]], used [[nuclear magnetic resonance]] (NMR) spectroscopy and [[magic angle spinning]] (MAS) to study [[rare-earth]] [[pyrochlore]]s.<ref name=greydphil>{{cite thesis|degree=DPhil|publisher=University of Oxford|url=http://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/OXVU1:LSCOP_OX:oxfaleph015999547|title=A <sup>119</sup>Sn and <sup>89</sup>Y MAS NMR study of rare-Earth pyrochlores|first=Clare Philomena|last=Grey|date=1990|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.276535}}|website=bodleian.ox.ac.uk|oclc=53567496|access-date=1 March 2018|archive-date=13 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191213092833/http://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/OXVU1:LSCOP_OX:oxfaleph015999547|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Following Grey's graduate studies, she held a [[postdoctoral research]] position at the [[University of Nijmegen]].<ref name=":1" /> From 1992 to 1993, she worked as a visiting researcher at [[DuPont]].<ref name=":1" /> In 1994, Grey was appointed a professor at the [[State University of New York at Stony Brook]], and became full professor in 2001.<ref name=":1" /> In 2009, she became the Geoffrey Moorhouse Gibson Professor in Materials Chemistry at the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name=":1" />

From 2009 to 2010 she was the Director of the Northeastern Chemical Energy Storage Center, and Associate Director from 2011 to 2014. She is current the director of the EPSRC Centre for Advanced Materials for Integrated Systems.<ref name=":0" />

=== Battery research ===
Grey pioneered the application of [[nuclear magnetic resonance]] to study and improve the performance of batteries, particularly [[lithium ion batteries]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.materialstoday.com/view/10581/improved-lithium-batteries/|title=Improved lithium batteries - Materials Today|publisher=}}</ref> She also made major contributions to the development of [[Lithium–air battery|lithium-air batteries]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=New batteries for more climate protection|url=https://www.koerber-stiftung.de/en/new-batteries-for-more-climate-protection-2394|access-date=22 June 2021|website=www.koerber-stiftung.de|language=en-EN}}</ref>

Grey is co-founder of [[Nyobolt]], a company which specializes in [[niobium]]-based batteries.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nyobolt kickstarts niobium-based electric battery future with $10m fundraise|url=https://www.cambridgeindependent.co.uk/business/nyobolt-kickstarts-niobium-based-electric-battery-future-with-10m-fundraise-9159195/|url-status=live|access-date=22 June 2021|website=Cambridge Independent|date=8 March 2021 |language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210310131716/https://www.cambridgeindependent.co.uk/business/nyobolt-kickstarts-niobium-based-electric-battery-future-with-10m-fundraise-9159195/ |archive-date=10 March 2021 }}</ref>

===Honours and awards===
Grey was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) in 2011<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Clare Grey {{!}} Royal Society|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/clare-grey-11541/|access-date=22 June 2021|website=royalsociety.org|language=en-gb}}</ref> and awarded the [[Günther Laukien Prize]] in 2013<ref name=tr/> followed by the [[Davy Medal]] in 2014 for "''further pioneering applications of solid state nuclear magnetic resonance to materials of relevance to energy and the environment''."<ref name=":2" />

She was appointed [[Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (DBE) in the [[2022 Birthday Honours]] for services to science.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=63714|supp=y|page=B9|date=1 June 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Brackley |first=Mark |date=1 June 2022 |title=Queen's Jubilee Birthday Honours List 2022: All those honoured in Cambridgeshire as Prof Clare Grey is made a dame |url=https://www.cambridgeindependent.co.uk/news/queen-s-jubilee-birthday-honours-list-2022-all-those-honour-9257353/ |work=Cambridge Independent |location= |access-date=2 June 2022}}</ref>

In December 2013, Grey was awarded an Honorary Doctorate by [[Lancaster University]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=University |first=Lancaster |title=Honorary degree for Cambridge scientist {{!}} Lancaster University |url=https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/news/articles/2013/honorary-degree-for-cambridge-scientist/ |access-date=2025-03-27 |website=www.lancaster.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref>

Other awards, honours and career highlights include:

*2008 Vaughan Lecturer<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://rockychem.com/honors/vaughan-lecturer.html|title=Vaughan Lecturer {{!}} Rocky Mountain Conference|website=rockychem.com|date=28 October 2011 |access-date=29 June 2019}}</ref>
*2010 John Jeyes Award from the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ampere.ethz.ch/ampere_prize_2010.htm|title=AMPERE Prize 2010|website=ampere.ethz.ch|access-date=1 February 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202115558/http://www.ampere.ethz.ch/ampere_prize_2010.htm|archive-date=2 February 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*2011 [[Kavli Medal]]<ref name=Kavli>{{cite web| url=http://royalsociety.org/events/2011/following-function-real-time/ |title=Following function in real time| publisher=Royal Society| date=6 October 2011| access-date=5 October 2018}}</ref>
*2013 [[Günther Laukien Prize]]<ref name=tr>[http://www.theresonance.com/2013/categories/material-science/enc-monday-laukien-prize-2013 ENC Monday Bruker Party, Laukien Prize Awarded To Clare Grey | TheResonance – Bruker's Blog about NMR, EPR and MRI<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131012041742/http://www.theresonance.com/2013/categories/material-science/enc-monday-laukien-prize-2013 |date=12 October 2013 }}</ref>
*2015 Arfvedson-Schlenk Award,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/news/clare-grey-wins-arfvedson-schlenk-award|title=Clare Grey wins Arfvedson-Schlenk Award {{!}} Department of Chemistry|website=www.ch.cam.ac.uk|access-date=29 June 2019}}</ref> for outstanding scientific and technical achievements in lithium chemistry
*2017 Prix Franco-Britannique from the [[Société Chimique de France]]<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.societechimiquedefrance.fr/La-SCF-vient-d-attribuer-ses-Grands-Prix-et-Prix-binationaux-2017.html?lang=fr |title=La SCF vient d'attribuer ses Grands Prix et Prix binationaux 2017| publisher=Société Chimique de France |date=June 2017| access-date= 5 January 2019}}</ref>
* 2018 Interviewed by [[Jim Al-Khalili]] for ''[[The Life Scientific]]'' on [[BBC Radio 4]] first broadcast March 2018<ref name=tls>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b09tdr0r|website=bbc.co.uk|publisher=[[BBC]]|location=London|title=Clare Grey on the Big Battery Challenge|first=Jim|last=Al-Khalili|year=2018}}</ref>
*2019 [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] [[John B. Goodenough Award]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/JohnBGoodenoughAward/2019-Winner.asp|title=RSC John B Goodenough Award 2019 Winner|website=www.rsc.org|access-date=29 June 2019}}</ref>
*2020 [[Royal Society]] [[Hughes Medal]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hughes Medal {{!}} Royal Society|url=https://royalsociety.org/grants-schemes-awards/awards/hughes-medal/|access-date=4 August 2020|website=royalsociety.org|language=en-gb}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Hughes Medal recognises Grey's energy research |url=https://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/news/hughes-medal-recognises-greys-energy-research |access-date=8 April 2025 |agency=University of Cambridge |publisher=Yusuf Hamied Department of Chemistry |date=3 August 2020}}</ref>
*2021 [[Körber European Science Prize]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Clare Grey – Prizewinner 2021|url=https://www.koerber-stiftung.de/en/koerber-european-science-prize/previous-prizewinners/2021|access-date=22 June 2021|website=[[Körber Foundation]]|language=en-gb}}</ref>
